title: Cohomology of the base change map through the Kunneth identification
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed], let $n\geq1$ be an integer invertible in $K$, and put $A=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$. Let $j:U\to X$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] of schemes of finite type over $K$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $Y$ be projective over $K$ [def-kun-projective], and let $F$ be a sheaf of $A$-modules on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, viewed in degree zero in the ordinary module derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Put $Z=Y\times_KX$ and $W=Y\times_KU$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $r:Z\to Y$, $q:Z\to X$, $s:W\to Y$, $p:W\to U$, and $h=1_Y\times j:W\to Z$. Thus $qh=jp$ and $rh=s$.

Write $\Ex:q^{-1}Rj_*F\to Rh_*p^{-1}F$ for the exchange of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. All tensor products below are derived over $A$ [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Let $E=\underline A_Y$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. The external-product maps of [def-kun-kunneth-map], with the pullback-of-constant and tensor-unit identifications, give the Kunneth isomorphisms [lem-kun-0f14b]
$$
 k_Z:R\Gamma(Y,E)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}R\Gamma(X,Rj_*F)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(Z,q^{-1}Rj_*F),
$$
$$
 k_W:R\Gamma(Y,E)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}R\Gamma(U,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(W,p^{-1}F).
$$
Let $\lambda_j:R\Gamma(X,Rj_*F)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(U,F)$ and $\lambda_h:R\Gamma(Z,Rh_*p^{-1}F)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(W,p^{-1}F)$ be the canonical module-valued Leray comparisons: the inverses of the derived direct-image composition comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], normalized by the composite adjunction as in [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition]. Then
$$
 \lambda_h\circ R\Gamma(Z,\Ex)\circ k_Z
 =k_W\circ(1_{R\Gamma(Y,E)}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\lambda_j).
$$
Equivalently, under these two Kunneth identifications and the Leray identifications, $R\Gamma(Z,\Ex)$ is the identity of $R\Gamma(Y,\underline A_Y)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}R\Gamma(U,F)$.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$. By [lem-kun-0ezp] every object of $S_{\Et}$ is a disjoint union of copies of $S$. The sheaf axiom identifies a module sheaf with $V\mapsto M^{\pi_0(V)}$, where $M$ is its value at $S$, and morphisms with $A$-linear maps of $M$. Thus evaluation and constant sheaf are inverse exact equivalences with $A$-modules. The tensor comparison is the identity at $S$, hence an isomorphism; apply the exact equivalences termwise to obtain the derived equivalence. For the structure map $a_T:T\to S$, evaluation of $a_{T*}$ at $S$ is global sections by definition, so under this equivalence $Ra_{T*}=R\Gamma(T,-)$, with its $A$-action retained.

source.place: Tag 0EZP, lemma-vanishing-irreducible; specialization to the separably closed point and elementary sheaf gluing

proof.text: Write $a:Y\to S$, $b:X\to S$, $c=bj:U\to S$, $d=bq:Z\to S$, and $e=dh=cp:W\to S$. Set $H=Rj_*F$, $P=Ra_*E$, $B=Rb_*H$, and $C=Rc_*F$. Use the inverse composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] for $(j,b)$ and $(h,d)$ to define $\lambda_j:B\to C$ and $\lambda_h:Rd_*Rh_*p^{-1}F\to Re_*p^{-1}F$. The sites may be replaced by small representatives in a larger universe; the ring on each is the constant $A$, and the structural ring maps are the pullback-of-constant isomorphisms. All derived inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions are those fixed by [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. Their composition maps are the unit-normalized module maps of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear], descended termwise as in [def-kun-kunneth-map]. The normalization in the composition statement agrees with the right-adjoint comparison as follows. For either inner map $f=j$ or $f=h$, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applies because $f^{-1}$ is exact, so $f_*I$ is K-injective whenever $I$ is. Thus in the normalization one may take $J=f_*I$ and the resolution map to be the identity. On these representatives, the comparison is the ordinary direct-image composition identification and its adjunction is the composite of the two ordinary Hom bijections. Consequently [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] identifies its counit with the pasted counit. Naturality of the resolution identifications gives this normalization for every derived object.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, canonical comparison; exact-adjoint K-injective specialization

proof.text:
With the canonical inverse-image composition identifications understood, this gives the two typed identities
$$
 \varepsilon_{c,F}\circ c^{-1}(\lambda_j)
 =\varepsilon_{j,F}\circ j^{-1}(\varepsilon_{b,H})
 :c^{-1}B\longrightarrow F,
$$
$$
 \varepsilon_{e,p^{-1}F}\circ e^{-1}(\lambda_h)
 =\varepsilon_{h,p^{-1}F}\circ h^{-1}(\varepsilon_{d,Rh_*p^{-1}F}).
$$
These formulas fix the actual Leray maps and their directions, not just isomorphisms of their endpoints.

By [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], $Y$ is proper over $K$. Thus [lem-kun-0f14b] applies to $(Y,X,E,H)$ and $(Y,U,E,F)$: $K$ is separably closed, $n$ is invertible, $X$ and $U$ are finite type, and both $H$ and $F$ belong to the stated unbounded $A$-module categories. No constructibility or separatedness of $X$ is required. By [lem-kun-pullback-constant], $r^{-1}E=A_Z$ and $s^{-1}E=A_W$ canonically. The left unit constraints of [lem-kun-tensor-unit] therefore give isomorphisms
$$u_Z:r^{-1}E\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}q^{-1}H\to q^{-1}H,
\qquad u_W:s^{-1}E\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}p^{-1}F\to p^{-1}F.$$
In the notation of [def-kun-kunneth-map], the maps in the statement are precisely $k_Z=Rd_*(u_Z)\circ\kappa_{E,H}$ and $k_W=Re_*(u_W)\circ\kappa_{E,F}$. Both are invertible.

source.place: Tag 0F14, lemma-kunneth-one-proper (2), applied with proper Y; projective implies proper: Tag 01WC

proof.text:
The current definition fixes the comparison
$$
 t_Z=(\gamma_{a,r,P}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\gamma_{b,q,B})\circ(\mu^d_{P,B})^{-1}
 :d^{-1}(P\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B)\longrightarrow r^{-1}a^{-1}P\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}q^{-1}b^{-1}B.
$$
Here $\gamma_{a,r}:d^{-1}\to r^{-1}a^{-1}$ and $\gamma_{b,q}:d^{-1}\to q^{-1}b^{-1}$ are exactly its termwise-descended constant-coefficient module composition maps. Thus the transpose of $k_Z$ is
$$u_Z\circ(r^{-1}\varepsilon_{a,E}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}q^{-1}\varepsilon_{b,H})\circ t_Z.$$
For any $L,M\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ put
$$t_W(L,M)=(\gamma_{a,s,L}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\gamma_{c,p,M})\circ(\mu^e_{L,M})^{-1}.
$$
The transpose of $k_W$ is
$$u_W\circ(s^{-1}\varepsilon_{a,E}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}p^{-1}\varepsilon_{c,F})\circ t_W(P,C).$$ These are the maps obtained from the definition's explicit unit-then-direct-image formula for $\kappa$, under its canonical K-injective Hom bijection.

Canonical tensor and composition identifications in the double-adjoint calculation

proof.text:
Let $D=P\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$, $Q=q^{-1}H$, and $V=p^{-1}F$. Write $\alpha_Z=u_Z\circ(r^{-1}\varepsilon_{a,E}\otimes q^{-1}\varepsilon_{b,H})\circ t_Z$, the transpose of $k_Z$ from step 5. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], the Hom bijection for $h^{-1}d^{-1}\dashv Rd_*Rh_*$ is the composite of the two Hom bijections. The normalization in steps 2–3 identifies this with $e^{-1}\dashv Re_*$ through $\gamma_{d,h}$ and $\lambda_h$. Apply the inverse-Hom formula $\Psi^{-1}(f)=\varepsilon\circ L(f)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] first for $d$ and then for $h$. Naturality of $\varepsilon_d$ moves $\Ex:Q\to Rh_*V$ across the first formula. The transpose of $\lambda_h\circ Rd_*(\Ex)\circ k_Z$ is therefore
$$\varepsilon_{h,V}\circ h^{-1}(\Ex)\circ h^{-1}(\alpha_Z)\circ\gamma_{d,h,D}.$$
The defining mate formula of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] says $\varepsilon_{h,V}\circ h^{-1}(\Ex)=p^{-1}\varepsilon_{j,F}\circ\sigma_H$, where $\sigma:h^{-1}q^{-1}\to p^{-1}j^{-1}$ is step 6's square comparison.

source.place: Exchange counit route; explicit composite Hom bijection and its naturality (Stacks categories.tex Tags 0037, definition-adjoint, and 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits)

proof.text:
Substitute $\alpha_Z$ into step 7. The tensor-composition and unit equations of [lem-kun-derived-pullback-composition-monoidal], in the instance displayed in step 6, move $h^{-1}$ through its two tensor factors and identify the pulled-back left unit with $u_W$. Naturality of the same composition comparisons moves the two counits through $\rho$ and $\sigma$. Hence the transpose of the left side is
$$u_W\circ(1\otimes p^{-1}\varepsilon_{j,F})\circ(s^{-1}\varepsilon_{a,E}\otimes p^{-1}j^{-1}\varepsilon_{b,H})\circ(1\otimes p^{-1}\gamma_{b,j,B})\circ t_W(P,B).$$
Every arrow has source or target among $e^{-1}D$, $s^{-1}a^{-1}P\otimes p^{-1}c^{-1}B$, $s^{-1}a^{-1}P\otimes p^{-1}j^{-1}b^{-1}B$, $s^{-1}E\otimes p^{-1}j^{-1}H$, and $s^{-1}E\otimes p^{-1}F$, in that order. Thus this display retains the square and composition comparisons rather than suppressing them.

source.place: Exchange counit route; explicit composite Hom bijection and its naturality (Stacks categories.tex Tags 0037, definition-adjoint, and 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits)

proof.text:
By the precomposition naturality of the inverse Hom bijection in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] and the adjoint description of [def-kun-kunneth-map], the transpose of $k_W\circ(1_P\otimes\lambda_j)$ is
$$u_W\circ(s^{-1}\varepsilon_{a,E}\otimes p^{-1}\varepsilon_{c,F})\circ t_W(P,C)\circ e^{-1}(1_P\otimes\lambda_j).$$
Bifunctoriality of the tensor comparison [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] and naturality of the composition comparisons in [def-kun-kunneth-map] give
$$t_W(P,C)\circ e^{-1}(1_P\otimes\lambda_j)=(1\otimes p^{-1}c^{-1}\lambda_j)\circ t_W(P,B).$$
Consequently the right transpose is
$$u_W\circ\bigl(s^{-1}\varepsilon_{a,E}\otimes p^{-1}(\varepsilon_{c,F}\circ c^{-1}\lambda_j)\bigr)\circ t_W(P,B).$$

source.place: Exchange counit route; explicit composite Hom bijection and its naturality (Stacks categories.tex Tags 0037, definition-adjoint, and 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits)

proof.text:
Restore the composition comparison in the first counit identity of step 3:
$$\varepsilon_{c,F}\circ c^{-1}\lambda_j=\varepsilon_{j,F}\circ j^{-1}(\varepsilon_{b,H})\circ\gamma_{b,j,B}.$$
This is the pasted-counit formula of [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition]. Substitute it into the last display of step 9 and use bifunctoriality of tensor. The result is precisely step 8's display, with the same $t_W(P,B)$ and the same $\gamma_{b,j,B}$. The two transposes are equal, and the Hom bijection is injective, so the equality in the statement follows.

source.place: Exchange counit route; explicit composite Hom bijection and its naturality (Stacks categories.tex Tags 0037, definition-adjoint, and 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits)

proof.text:
The common source can now be identified with $P\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}C$ by $1_P\otimes\lambda_j$. The equality of step 10 reads
$$k_W^{-1}\circ\lambda_h\circ R\Gamma(Z,\Ex)\circ k_Z\circ(1_P\otimes\lambda_j)^{-1}=1_{P\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}C}.$$
Every inverse exists by steps 2 and 4. This is the claimed identity on $R\Gamma(Y,\underline A_Y)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}R\Gamma(U,F)$.
